window.input: Get a shower and get changed for the quiz
window.narration: You gather the tools and head out, pulling Nia's door to behind you. The bathroom is free — a minor miracle. The shower takes thirty seconds to settle on something tolerable, then spends the rest of the time oscillating between lukewarm and aggressive. You manage. By ten past five you're back in your room, Harrington jacket on over a clean shirt, the overcoat hung on the back of the door in reserve. You look presentable. More to the point, you look like you didn't try too hard.

Your phone buzzes. Aisha, from downstairs: *'Buyer confirmed. Says he can do 6pm, outside the Co-op on Uplands Crescent. I'll come with you if you want — got the listing on my phone.'* Downstairs the front door opens and closes; the letting agent gone, by the sound of it. Half five. Plenty of time before the quiz.

window.input: Go with aisha and meet them
window.narration: You shout down to Aisha that you're coming. She appears at the foot of the stairs already in her coat, the Marketplace listing pulled up on her phone. You unearth the Kenwood mixer from your room — still in its original carry position, awkward but manageable — and the two of you head out into the early evening. Uplands Crescent is five minutes on foot. The Co-op forecourt smells of cardboard and cold air.

window.input: Wait by the entrance and watch for him
window.narration: You set the mixer down by the Co-op entrance and lean against the wall. A bloke in a Ford Focus circles twice before pulling over — late twenties, fleece, the careful look of someone who's done a few Marketplace deals before. He gets out, glances at the box, picks it up, sets it down, plugs nothing into nothing but lifts the lid and peers inside. 'Does it all work?' 'Aye,' says Aisha, without looking up from her phone. He counts out thirty without being asked.

window.input: Walk back and chat it aisha
window.narration: You fall into step beside Aisha, heading back up the Crescent. The streetlights are coming on in that half-hearted way they do in early October — not quite needed yet, not quite useless. 'Thirty,' she says. 'Told you it'd go.' She sounds satisfied without sounding smug, which is a skill. She asks if you've decided on a specialist subject for the quiz.

window.input: Say im winging it and give her a fiver for her cut
window.narration: 'Winging it,' you say. 'Bit of everything. Hoping for the best.' Aisha gives you a look that contains a full paragraph of scepticism. You pull a fiver from your wallet and hold it out. 'Your cut. For the listing.' She glances at it, then takes it without ceremony. 'You're buying me a drink at the quiz instead.' She doesn't say thank you, which somehow makes it feel more genuine.

window.input: Ill buy you a drink no problem aisha, hinting she wants more than just a drink
window.narration: Aisha slows her pace just slightly. 'Just a drink,' she says, which is exactly what someone says when they mean something more ambiguous than that. She doesn't look at you when she says it. The Co-op's fluorescent glow fades behind you and the Crescent opens up into the quieter stretch toward home. 'Quiz starts at seven,' she adds, businesslike again. 'Don't be late or Nia'll have you doing sport.'

window.input: Walk with her in comfortable silence
window.narration: Neither of you fills the gap. The Crescent is quiet enough that you can hear her keys jangling in her coat pocket. A cat — probably Owen's — sits on the wall outside number fourteen and watches you pass with the mild contempt of something that has never had to split a utility bill. The house comes into view. Lights on in the kitchen.

window.input: Head up to your room to drop the rucksack before the quiz
window.narration: You take the stairs two at a time. Your room is exactly as you left it — which is to say, not quite tidy but not embarrassing. You shrug off the rucksack and drop it by the desk, peel off the overcoat and drape it over the chair. Feels lighter already. The quiz is in just over half an hour; there's enough time to not rush.

window.input: Head straight back down and rally the team
window.narration: You clatter back downstairs. The kitchen light's on — Tomos is at the counter with a mug, Aisha's just come in behind you, and Nia appears from the hallway already in her jacket, bag over one shoulder. 'Right,' she says, taking in the assembled group. 'Rhys is meeting us there. That's five. We going?' Tomos drains his mug. Nobody argues. The Westbourne is a ten-minute walk.

window.input: Ask if anyone's sorted a sixth player, check messages on the phone
window.narration: Nia's already heading for the door. 'Sixth?' you say, pulling your phone out. 'Did anyone grab someone else?' Tomos shrugs. Aisha says she mentioned it to a girl from her seminar but got no reply. Nia pauses, hand on the latch. 'Cerys said five's fine. Six is better but it's not a rule.' Your phone shows nothing useful — no new messages, no Marketplace pings since Aisha's overnight batch. Just a news notification you'll never read.

window.input: Head to the Westbourne with everyone now
window.narration: Nia pulls the front door open and the evening air comes in — damp, faintly beery, proper October. You fall in behind her. Tomos and Aisha follow. The five of you head up the Crescent in a loose group, nobody walking too fast. The Westbourne's windows are already warm and lit against the dark. Rhys is outside under the hanging basket, hands in his pockets, looking like he wasn't sure you'd actually show.
